answer: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) goes in the burette; the flask holds the acid plus a few drops of phenolphthalein indicator.
Early on, pink flashes where the sodium hydroxide lands, then fades as you swirl, so you can add it quickly.
Slow down to drop by drop when the pink starts to linger instead of fading.
The endpoint is a faint pink that lasts thirty seconds.
Stop adding sodium hydroxide, then read the volume (on the burette; the picture shows a 0 reading marker, but the clip does not say how to read it).
